title: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: Economy growth 2015 and 2016
sections.summary: The economy grew 2% in 2015 and is expected to grow between 1% and 3% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The economy grew by 2% in 2015 and we are expected to grow between 1% and 3% in 2016.

sections.label: Manufacturing sector in recession
sections.summary: The manufacturing sector is in recession, recording a 6.7% contraction in the last quarter of 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Well, the manufacturing sector is already in recession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It recorded its weakest performance in the last quarter of 2015, with a contraction of 6.7%.

sections.label: Services sector growth and constraints
sections.summary: The services sector grew 2.8% in the last quarter but faces supply side constraints and margin squeeze.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The services sector, which is more domestic-focused, grew at a moderate pace of 2.8% in the last quarter but the sector is faced with supply side constraints and margin squeeze.

sections.label: Schemes helping companies internationalise
sections.summary: Enhancements to existing schemes and new schemes were announced to help companies which are internationalising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To the credit of MTI and International Enterprise (IE) Singapore, several enhancements to existing schemes were announced last year, such as the Market Readiness Assistance Scheme and the Global Company Partnership Scheme administered by IE Singapore and new schemes, like the International Growth Scheme, amongst others, introduced to help companies which are internationalising.

sections.label: SkillsFuture for workers' employability
sections.summary: SkillsFuture can be the immediate tool for workers to learn and safeguard employability throughout their work life cycle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture can be the immediate tool available to workers to learn and safeguard workers' employability throughout their work life cycle.

sections.label: Update on CFE progress
sections.summary: The Minister is asked for an update on the CFE's progress on criteria for attracting and incentivising inward foreign investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Could the Minister also provide an update on the progress of the CFE so far?

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This is on the Government's criteria which are used when attracting and incentivising inward foreign investments into Singapore.

sections.label: TPP signing and trade share
sections.summary: The TPP was signed on 4 February by 12 member countries, whose signatories comprise nearly 40% of world trade and over 30% of Singapore's total trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On 4 February this year, it was signed by 12 member countries − Singapore, the United States (US), Japan, Malaysia, Vietnam, Brunei, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Mexico, Chile and Peru.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Minister also noted that the TPP signatories comprise nearly 40% of world trade and account for more than 30% of Singapore's total trade.

sections.label: TPP benefits for workers
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to describe TPP benefits beyond existing free trade agreements and, beyond corporations, the benefits to Singapore workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Can the Minister describe exactly what benefits the TPP will usher in beyond the various free trade agreements and economic partnerships that Singapore currently already has?

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Most importantly, beyond benefits for corporations, what are the benefits to Singapore workers?

sections.label: Services trade performance and outlook
sections.summary: Services export grew about 200% from 2003 to 2013, the services trade balance turned negative around 2000, and MTI's outlook on recent agreements is asked.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Data from the Department of Statistics show that services export grew by about 200% over the period 2003 to 2013, compared to merchandise exports which only grew about 60% over the same period.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, the services trade balance turned negative around the year 2000 and has continued in negative territory for much of the time since.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2015, services trade performance deteriorated, with growth rates of both exports and imports almost flat.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is MTI's outlook on the impact that recent agreements, such as the ASEAN Economic Community and the TPP, will have on services trade performance?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have examined the drivers of services export.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We find that three areas which contributed quite significantly to the weak balance were telecommunications, computer and information, charges for the use of intellectual property, and research and development (R&D).

sections.label: Manufacturing importance and transformation
sections.summary: With GDP up 2% but manufacturing contracting 5.2%, the question asks the Government's view on manufacturing's importance and approach to helping it transform and compete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last year, notwithstanding that GDP for the whole economy has increased by 2%, the manufacturing sector has contracted by 5.2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The three sectors which have shown the highest growth rates are: (a) wholesale and retail trade, (b) finance and insurance and (c) information and communication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Given that Singapore has progressed to be a more services-oriented economy, I would like to ask what is the Government's view on the importance of manufacturing to Singapore's economy and what is our approach towards developing and helping the manufacturing sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the face of intensifying competition from the region, how can we help key manufacturing sectors transform, innovate, grow and compete globally?

sections.label: Heat and wrapper shelf life
sections.summary: Proper control of heat and choice of wrapper can increase product shelf life by 40% and provide reheating and microwavable options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Proper control of heat and choice of wrapper can increase the shelf life of products by 40% and also provide consumers reheating and microwavable options.

sections.label: Anti-competitive practices assurance
sections.summary: In his Budget round-up speech, the Finance Minister gave the assurance that anti-competitive practices will not be allowed to creep in.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: In his Budget round-up speech, the Finance Minister yesterday gave the assurance that anti-competitive practices will not be allowed to creep in.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme question
sections.summary: MOF announced the Industry Transformation Programme and MTI is asked how it differs and how sectors and companies benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) has announced the Industry Transformation Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For the public's benefits, can MTI share how this new approach is different from the current approach and how our sectors and companies will benefit?

sections.label: Startup ecosystem progress question
sections.summary: The passage asks about progress in developing a startup ecosystem and whether more support is planned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What is the progress of the Government's efforts to develop a startup ecosystem and does the Government plan to do more to support the growth of startups in Singapore?

sections.label: Mentoring incentives for entrepreneurs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will consider incentives for those willing to guide budding entrepreneurs and technopreneurs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With this, we can start an ecosystem where a buddy-and-mentor relationship can be forged within the startup.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, my question here, Ministers, is: will the Ministry be willing to consider and provide incentives to professionals, companies and voluntary organisations which are willing to come forward to guide and mentor these budding entrepreneurs and technopreneurs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Budget 2016 has set up a new working capital loan scheme with 50% risk-sharing.

sections.label: Financing expectations survey index
sections.summary: An SBF-DP Info survey last year found the index for financing access expectations fell to its lowest since 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In a Singapore Business Federation (SBF)-DP Info survey last year, the index measuring expectations for access to financing fell to its lowest levels since 2013.

sections.label: SME capital access and EXIM
sections.summary: The passage states access to capital warrants analysis and review of counter measures, including the EXIM bank idea, for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Access to capital is an issue that warrants both fact-based analysis and review of counter measures, including the EXIM bank idea, if our SMEs, which account for two-thirds of employment, are to maintain and create jobs for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Securing Singapore IP rights
sections.summary: The passage asks what requirements ensure Singapore's rights to IP created through its funding are adequately secured.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Because it is intimately and ultimately affecting the flow-through from our research, the flow-through to Singapore, which is why I would like to know the requirements in place, or the requirements that will be in place, to ensure that Singapore's rights to IP created through its funding are adequately secured.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to clarify that when I refer to Singapore, I am not referring to the Government alone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am not arguing that all IP rights must be owned by the Singapore Government, but rather that the IP rights must be owned within Singapore, whether it is the Government, industry, enterprise or individuals.

sections.label: Industry role in RIE2020
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister whether Budget 2016 incorporated companies, especially SMEs, leveraging RIE2020 to innovate and create value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Last, but not least, I would be grateful if the Minister could comment on the structured framework suggested in my speech during the debate, that is, for the larger involvement of industry as client, rather than feedback provider, and as IP owner and recipient of research grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So my question is: has Budget 2016 already incorporated the fact that companies, especially SMEs, have the possibility of leveraging on RIE2020 to innovate and create value?

sections.label: Access to research institutes
sections.summary: Measures could include easier access to R&D institutes, polytechnic research units and unused IP technology, and lower-cost laboratory tests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Some measures could include giving them easier access to R&D institutes, polytechnic research units and usage of unused IP technology so that they can enhance their business, and to conduct laboratory tests, for example, at lower costs at our research institutes or polytechnics.

sections.label: Social robotics in Singapore
sections.summary: NUS and other institutes have social robotics programmes, but Singapore has yet to bring a commercially successful social robot product to market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The National University of Singapore and other institutes have social robotics programmes but, to the best of my knowledge, Singapore has yet to bring to market a commercially successful social robot product to compete with, for example, Pepper, the iconic social robot from Japan, which is now selling around 1,000 units per month, even though it is not Jarvis.

sections.label: Social robots for eldercare
sections.summary: Singapore is well-placed to prototype and test bed social robots for eldercare and preschool markets, and a report said nuclear energy was not yet suitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Even though the Japanese seem to have a lead in this space, Mdm Chairperson, Singapore is well-placed to prototype and test bed social robots for the eldercare and preschool markets in Asia, given the Asian multi-ethnic and multilingual nature of our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I hope this is an area that can receive attention from policymakers and be a subject of collaboration between local enterprises and the R&D sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In it, they recommended that nuclear energy was currently not yet suitable for Singapore, but that we needed to "keep our options open for the future".

sections.label: Nuclear research training shortfall
sections.summary: The programme aims to train about 10 people a year toward 100 nuclear experts in 10 years, but trained nine in two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It aims to train about 10 people a year to produce about 100 nuclear experts at the end of 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, in two years of operation, the research programme has only managed to train nine people, which is fewer than the target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Over the years we have reduced our dependency on oil and have increased our use of natural gas for power generation, from 74.4% in 2005 to 95.5% in 2015.

sections.label: Retail electricity market liberalisation
sections.summary: Mr Iswaran announced Singapore's retail electricity market will be fully liberalised in the second half of 2018, letting 1.3 million users choose a supplier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Iswaran, Minister for Trade, announced last October that Singapore's retail electricity market will be fully liberalised in the second half of 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This will allow the remaining 1.3 million users, who are primarily domestic home users, to have the flexibility to choose a supplier according to their electricity usage habits.

sections.label: Renewable energy and solar power
sections.summary: Due to technical issues with other renewables, Singapore can rely mainly on solar power, potentially meeting up to 8% of peak demand by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We also need to find more environmentally friendly ways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, due to various technical issues with different forms of renewable energy resources, we can only really rely on solar power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is estimated that by 2030, we could potentially be tapping on renewable energy to contribute up to 8% of Singapore's peak electricity demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In addition to our focus on research to improve the performance of solar systems, what further steps are we taking to reach our renewable energy goals?

sections.label: Singapore economic growth forecast
sections.summary: Singapore's economic growth is expected to remain modest between 1% and 3% this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, we expect Singapore's economic growth to remain modest between 1% and 3% this year.

sections.label: SME Working Capital Loan
sections.summary: The SME Working Capital Loan gives SMEs unsecured working capital up to S$300,000, with the Government co-sharing 50% of default risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: First, given the tightening credit situation, we are introducing measures, such as the SME Working Capital Loan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: This will allow SMEs to access unsecured working capital of up to S$300,000 to complement existing financing schemes to support viable SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: As the Government will co-share 50% of the default risk of the loan portfolio with the participating financial institutions, we expect this to catalyse approximately $2 billion of total loans to companies over the next three years.

sections.label: Facilities ready this year
sections.summary: Facilities ready this year include Aviation Two @ Seletar Aerospace Park, Chemicals Hub @ Tuas South, Space @ Gul and Space @ Tampines North.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Some of the facilities that will be ready this year include Aviation Two @ Seletar Aerospace Park, Chemicals Hub @ Tuas South, Space @ Gul and Space @ Tampines North.

sections.label: New LEAD+ programme for TACs
sections.summary: A new LEAD+ programme will help TACs strengthen in-house capabilities in four ways, as they are constrained by limited resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: TACs can do more and, in fact, they want to do more, but are constrained by their limited resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: This is why we are introducing a new LEAD+ programme, which will help TACs to strengthen in-house capabilities in four ways.

sections.label: Seconding officers to TACs
sections.summary: The Government is prepared to second up to 20 Public Service officers over the next five years to TACs under the LEAD+ programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: The Government is also prepared to second up to 20 Public Service officers over the next five years to TACs under this LEAD+ programme.

sections.label: TAC Collaborative Industry Projects
sections.summary: TACs will drive 30 Collaborative Industry Projects over three years, sourcing scalable solutions for industry productivity and innovation, benefiting over 3,000 SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Apart from strengthening TACs' capabilities, we will also partner TACs to drive 30 Collaborative Industry Projects (TAC-CIP) over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: TACs will source for bottom-up, scalable solutions to industry-specific productivity and innovation needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: We expect this programme to benefit over 3,000 SMEs.

sections.label: Expected productivity and safety outcomes
sections.summary: Expected outcomes include a 25% increase in each truck's productivity, better working conditions, manpower retention and improved workplace safety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Expected outcomes include a 25% increase in productivity of each truck, improvement in working conditions and, therefore, manpower retention, as well as improvement in workplace safety.

sections.label: Services exports growth 2010 to 2014
sections.summary: From 2010 to 2014, services exports grew 8.6% on a compound annual growth rate basis and remain a good engine of growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: In fact, over the period 2010 to 2014, our services exports have actually recorded robust growth of 8.6% on a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) basis and continue to be a good engine of growth.

sections.label: TPP market access and auto parts
sections.summary: The TPP improves market access beyond bilateral agreements, giving Singapore direct access to NAFTA markets and helping automotive parts manufacturers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Regional trade deals like the TPP enable us to improve our market access beyond what we already have under our bilateral trade agreements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: This is because the US also has the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which has created a very competitive automotive supply chain amongst the US, Canada and Mexico.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: However, when the TPP enters into force, Singapore will have direct access to all the NAFTA markets and, because the rules are applied commonly to all TPP countries, Singapore automotive parts manufacturers may become a competitive supplier of auto parts to TPP countries over time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: With the TPP, however, more of the raw materials that we process will count towards being "TPP or Singapore made".

sections.label: MTI engaging businesses on TPP
sections.summary: MTI has been actively engaging businesses on the benefits of the TPP through platforms such as the SME Convention 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: MTI has been actively engaging businesses on the benefits of the TPP through platforms such as the recent SME Convention 2016.

sections.label: Leveraging trends for growth areas
sections.summary: Growth areas must leverage key trends and strengths, and the Committee on the Future Economy was established to leverage these opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: Third, we need to leverage key trends and our strengths to develop growth areas that can create value, and invest in future growth engines to spur our economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
sentences.text: We must prepare ourselves for the future and the Committee on the Future Economy was, therefore, established to leverage these opportunities.

sections.label: Manufacturing real value-added growth
sections.summary: Manufacturing real value-added rose by $4.6 billion over the period, though growth was slightly lower than in 2010.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Though that is slightly lower than in 2010, largely due to the relatively faster growth of financial and insurance services, amongst others, the real value-added of the manufacturing sector, in fact, increased by $4.6 billion over the same period.

sections.label: Manufacturing productivity per hour
sections.summary: From 2009 to 2015, real value-added per actual hour worked in the sector grew 6.1% annually, above the economy's 2.7%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: From 2009 to 2015, the real value-added per actual hour worked in the sector grew by 6.1% per annum, higher than the 2.7% which is for the overall economy.

sections.label: Manufacturing spillover to economy
sections.summary: MTI estimates a $1 billion rise in manufacturing value-added from final demand generates about $300 million value-added and 2,400 jobs elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Based on MTI's estimates, a $1 billion increase in manufacturing value-added due to an increase in final demand will generate about $300 million of value-added and 2,400 jobs in the rest of the economy.

sections.label: National Robotics Programme investment
sections.summary: Over $450 million will be invested through the National Robotics Programme in end-to-end development of robotics technology.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To seize this opportunity, we will invest over $450 million through the National Robotics Programme (NRP) in the end-to-end development of robotics technology.

sections.label: Modular robotics for SMEs
sections.summary: EDB and SPRING work with local partners on standardised modular robotics solutions, letting SMEs mix modules and cutting adoption cost about 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In fact, EDB and the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING) are working with technology partners and system integrators locally to develop standardised and scalable modular robotics solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This will allow SMEs to mix and match these modules to suit their needs and, importantly, the cost of adoption can also be reduced by about 50%.

sections.label: Robots deployed in hotel
sections.summary: With STB support, two robots will be deployed from July this year at Park Avenue Rochester Hotel for housekeeping and back-of-house functions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Similarly, with the Singapore Tourism Board's (STB's) support, two robots will be deployed from July this year in Park Avenue Rochester Hotel for housekeeping and back-of-house functions, such as transportation of linen, refuse and bulky items.

sections.label: Eastern Health Alliance tele-health programme
sections.summary: EDB and MOH supported the Eastern Health Alliance's innovation team at Changi General Hospital, which partnered Philips Healthcare on a tele-health programme for heart failure patients.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: EDB and the Ministry of Health supported the Eastern Health Alliance to establish their innovation team at Changi General Hospital to work with the industry and test-bed new healthcare solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This team partnered Philips Healthcare to jointly develop a tele-health programme for heart failure patients in Singapore, to care for their health and, more importantly, to reduce the risk of re-admission via tele-monitoring, education and customised care plans.

sections.label: Physical proximity and Jurong Innovation District
sections.summary: Physical proximity encourages interaction among enterprises, solution providers and researchers, as at one-north, and the Jurong Innovation District can do the same for manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Physical proximity is one means to encourage greater interaction among enterprises, solution providers and researchers that can spark novel ideas and create new products.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We have done this at one-north, which is home to some 250 leading companies and global institutions, many incubators, startups and public research institutes and they, collectively, create about 40,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Jurong Innovation District (JID) can do the same for the manufacturing sector, with several new growth areas that can be housed there, for example, advanced manufacturing, robotics which I mentioned, urban solutions, cleantech and also smart logistics as an extension.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: JTC LaunchPad @ JID will be ready in 2017 to support startups, incubators and accelerators.

sections.label: Precision Engineering Master Craftsmen Programme
sections.summary: In 2012 Mr Jamil enrolled in Nanyang Polytechnic's Precision Engineering Master Craftsmen Programme, and now oversees the mold-making team and facilitates automation of machining processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In 2012, he enrolled in the Precision Engineering Master Craftsmen Programme conducted by Nanyang Polytechnic where he acquired technical skills, such as machining process design.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Upon graduation with the Workforce Skills Qualification (WSQ) Diploma in Precision Engineering Master Craftsmen Skill and a WSQ Specialist Diploma in Precision Engineering, Mr Jamil now oversees the mold-making team and facilitates the automation of machining processes.

sections.label: Partnerships for Capability Transformation scheme
sections.summary: Singapore has encouraged partnerships among diverse stakeholders, supporting natural partners through schemes such as the Partnerships for Capability Transformation, where large enterprises upgrade suppliers' capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Yet, if we look at our track record and experience, we have always encouraged and nurtured close partnerships among quite diverse stakeholders in our economic system; some of them are "natural partners" and others could even be competitors.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We have supported "natural partners" through schemes, such as the Partnerships for Capability Transformation (PACT), where large enterprises upgrade their suppliers' capabilities, through sourcing and qualification processes, and that is mutually beneficial.

sections.label: Automation support funding elements
sections.summary: Over the next three years, $400 million of support will be available for more than 300 automation projects, comprising the enhanced CDG, the new 100% Investment Allowance and the enhanced LEFS.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Over the next three years, $400 million of support will be available for more than 300 automation projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This will comprise three elements: the enhanced Capability Development Grant (CDG) which supports 50% of full-scale automation project costs up to $1 million; the new 100% Investment Allowance (IA); and the enhanced Local Enterprise Finance Scheme (LEFS).

sections.label: Mr Tan's automation support grant
sections.summary: Under the enhanced Capability Development Grant, Mr Tan will receive a $1 million support grant and a 100% Investment Allowance on remaining capital investment of $900,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Under the enhanced Capability Development Grant, Mr Tan will receive a support grant of $1 million, defraying $100,000 of consultancy and installation fees, and $900,000 for the cost of capital investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And Mr Tan will also receive a 100% Investment Allowance on the remaining capital investment of $900,000, which will translate to about $153,000 of tax savings.

sections.label: Singapore startup and venture capital growth
sections.summary: Singapore startups more than doubled from 24,000 in 2005 to 55,000 in 2014, and venture capital deals doubled from about 70 in 2007 to 140 in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Over the years, startup activity has increased, with the number of startups in Singapore more than doubling from 24,000 in 2005 to 55,000 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The number of venture capitalist deals doubled from about 70 in 2007 to 140 in 2013, with aggregate deal value increasing seven-fold from $120 million to $860 million.

sections.label: Startup targeting glaucoma drugs market
sections.summary: Her startup attracted the world's top five pharmaceutical companies and will enter the global glaucoma drugs market worth US$4.3 billion, potentially benefiting up to 80 million patients by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Her startup has attracted the attention of the world's top five pharmaceutical companies and will make inroads into the global glaucoma drugs market worth US$4.3 billion, potentially benefiting up to 80 million glaucoma patients by 2020.

sections.label: IDP incubators and accelerators mentorship
sections.summary: Through 21 incubators and accelerators supported under IDP, about 90 industry professionals have been engaged to mentor and provide expertise to startups.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Through the 21 incubators and accelerators supported under IDP, about 90 industry professionals have been engaged to provide mentorship and expertise to our startups.

sections.label: Research scientist and engineer jobs
sections.summary: The number of research scientist and engineer jobs in Singapore increased from 19,000 in 2004 to 33,000 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: One measure is the number of research scientist and engineer jobs in Singapore, which has increased from 19,000 in 2004 to 33,000 in 2014.

sections.label: Business spending on R&D
sections.summary: Business spending on R&D doubled from $2.6 billion to $5.2 billion over the same 10-year period, catalysed by public spending on R&D.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Another measure is the business spending on R&D, which has doubled from $2.6 billion to $5.2 billion over the same 10-year period, catalysed by public spending on R&D.

sections.label: Biomedical sciences R&D initiative
sections.summary: The biomedical sciences R&D initiative launched in 2000 spawned a strong BMS sector, contributing over $12 billion in value-added and employing more than 18,000 people in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Our biomedical sciences (BMS) R&D initiative, which was launched in the 2000, has spawned a strong BMS sector, contributing over $12 billion in value-added (VA) and employing more than 18,000 people in 2014.

sections.label: IAF funding increase
sections.summary: Under RIE2020, IAF funding will be increased by $200 million to $1.8 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Under RIE2020, the IAF funding will be increased by $200 million to $1.8 billion.

sections.label: Intellectual Property Intermediary technology sourcing
sections.summary: The Intellectual Property Intermediary under A*STAR has helped companies source technologies locally and overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: One way is through the Intellectual Property Intermediary (IPI) under A*STAR, which has helped our companies source technologies locally and overseas.

sections.label: Researchers seconded to SMEs
sections.summary: To date, more than 600 researchers have been seconded to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To date, we have more than 600 researchers who have been seconded to SMEs.

sections.label: Terminal capacity expansion
sections.summary: The fourth tank could be completed by 2018, taking throughput capacity to 11 million tonnes per annum.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: That is a very important strategic step and something that should not be underestimated in terms of its value to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We have been expanding the terminal capacity and the fourth tank could be completed by 2018, which would take throughput capacity to 11 million tonnes per annum.

sections.label: Nuclear Safety Research and Education Programme
sections.summary: In April 2014, the Government announced a $63-million Nuclear Safety Research and Education Programme to support capability development.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In April 2014, the Government announced the plan for a $63-million Nuclear Safety Research and Education Programme to support capability development in this space.

sections.label: ASEAN nuclear emergency preparedness cooperation
sections.summary: Singapore works with ASEAN countries through ASEANTOM and IAEA to strengthen cooperation and share radiation monitoring data.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It is important that our region collectively build and strengthen our emergency preparedness and response as nuclear and radiological emergencies have basically no boundaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We are working with the ASEAN countries through the ASEAN Network of Regulatory Bodies of Atomic Energy (ASEANTOM) and IAEA to strengthen cooperation in this area and to share radiation monitoring data.

sections.label: Full retail electricity contestability by 2018
sections.summary: The plan is full retail contestability in the electricity market by 2018, with a comprehensive education programme needed before that.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As announced, the plan is to have full retail contestability in the electricity market by 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Certainly, well before we embark on that, we will need to have a comprehensive education programme to make sure households and individuals understand.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: First, we need to get the system right before we talk about communication.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme and entrepreneurship
sections.summary: It calls for proactive sectoral measures, with responses including the Industry Transformation Programme and efforts to boost entrepreneurship and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: It calls for proactive measures at the sectoral level, even as companies try and adapt to some of the challenges that they face.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, we are responding with efforts like the Industry Transformation Programme (ITP) and also through efforts to boost entrepreneurship and pervasive innovation in order to create value in the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I would conclude by saying that it is a formidable task but not insurmountable.

sections.label: 20 TAs industry transformation blueprints
sections.summary: Minister Heng Swee Keat announced 20 TAs would get Government assistance for industry transformation blueprints and officers seconded as industry leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A change in name or positioning of the organisation reflects the change in mindset of TA leaders and it is the first step to transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, when Minister Heng Swee Keat announced that 20 TAs would receive the Government's assistance to formulate their industry transformation blueprints, and that Government officers would be seconded as "industry leaders" to the various industries, many TAs started speculting on which would be the lucky ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am wondering how the knowledge and experience of the 20 officers would be applied to the TAs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a report by The Business Times, there are currently more than 350 TAs nationwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How can other TAs participate in this project after the 20 officers have been assigned?

sections.label: Well-performing TAs supported by agencies
sections.summary: TAs which have performed well are overwhelmingly sought after and supported by different Government agencies with assistance schemes and incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: TAs which have performed well are overwhelmingly sought after and supported by different Government agencies with various assistance schemes and incentives.

sections.label: Weak global growth and SME outlook
sections.summary: With weak global growth, the immediate business outlook for some SMEs and startups is still poor.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, while I am glad that both the Ministers have addressed some of the challenges and also some of the support packages or schemes that would be made available, but, with the weak global growth, the immediate business outlook for some of SMEs, as well as startups is still poor.

sections.label: Subsidised rental and tax rebate
sections.summary: The Government can consider providing subsidised rental and tax rebate for a fixed period based on mutually agreed objectives.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: The Government can consider providing some of their subsidised rental and tax rebate for a fixed period, based on some mutually agreed objectives, like innovative business models, target financial returns and others.

sections.label: Falling port and SME sentiment
sections.summary: Container volume fell 8.7% in 2015 and 9.7% in early 2016, while an SME sentiment index hit its lowest since 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: For instance, annual container volume handled at our ports for 2015 was 8.7% lower than for 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: Container volume handled in the first two months this year is 9.7% lower than for last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: The latest index by SBF and DP Information Group to measure business sentiment amongst SMEs showed that SMEs do not expect any growth during the next six months, with the Index at its lowest since it was first published in 2010.

sections.label: SME concerns on payouts and levies
sections.summary: SMEs are concerned about lower Productivity and Innovation Credit cash payouts and higher foreign worker levies, and the member asks what initiatives will help micro SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my speech during the Budget debate, they are concerned about the lowering of the cash payout rates for the Productivity and Innovation Credit Scheme and that the Government is proceeding with increasing the foreign worker levies for the services and construction sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Considering that micro SMEs will be hit the hardest during an economic slowdown, what initiatives will the Ministry be launching to help these smaller SMEs?

sections.label: SMEs share of workforce and GDP
sections.summary: SMEs hire two-thirds of the workforce and produce 50% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Our SMEs hire two-thirds of the workforce and produce 50% of our GDP.

sections.label: Productivity in outward and domestic sectors
sections.summary: Logistics and manufacturing saw 3.2% annual productivity growth over five years, while retail and F&B productivity fell about 0.6% yearly over three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Even as outward-oriented sectors, such as logistics and manufacturing, saw productivity growth of 3.2% each year over the last five years, in the domestically-oriented sectors, such as retail and F&B, productivity has fallen by about 0.6% each year in the last three years.

sections.label: Low productivity and high wages
sections.summary: Low productivity rates combined with disproportionately high wages are worrying and unsustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The low productivity rates, coupled with disproportionately high wages, are worrying as this situation is not sustainable.

sections.label: Funding for TACs questioned
sections.summary: The member asks what impact $7 million awarded to six TACs last year had, and whether new funding will add value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: In fact, just last year, Minister Lim Hng Kiang awarded further funding totalling $7 million to six TACs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister what impact has this support had over the last 10 years in helping TACs contribute meaningfully to the industries?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: How can we be sure that the additional funding this round that has been announced for TACs will, indeed, add value to the ground?

sections.label: Commercial and industrial rental increases
sections.summary: Calls on the Government to keep commercial and industrial rental increases near or below inflation and their absolute amounts manageable to nurture SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These now are significant expense items that breed insecurity for many small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We call on the Government to not only keep commercial and industrial rental increases near or below inflation but also keep their absolute amounts manageable as part of the more serious effort to nurture SMEs as the third pillar.

sections.label: HDB commercial space and rentals
sections.summary: Calls for increasing the supply of HDB commercial space and lowering rentals for HDB commercial properties to stimulate retail-oriented SME and startup businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, similarly increase the supply of HDB commercial space and lower the rentals for HDB commercial properties, which have increased substantially over the past 20 years, in order to stimulate retail-oriented businesses in the SME and startup sector and bring added diversity and vibrancy to our heartlands.

sections.label: Lowering JTC and HDB rentals
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government would consider leading in reducing business costs by lowering JTC and HDB industrial and commercial property rental rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Moving forward, should our domestic economy worsen considerably to warrant an off-Budget measure, and should our market rentals not adjust accordingly, would the Government consider taking the lead in reducing business costs by lowering JTC and HDB industrial and commercial property rental rates?

sections.label: Online purchases and refunds
sections.summary: Urges the Government to review online purchase legislation and give online consumers a right to return goods within seven days for a full refund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Another case involves a vendor who introduced pre-ticked boxes for consumers, making them sign up as a member paying monthly fees without the consumer realising it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to review the legislation regarding online purchases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Allow online consumers to be given a right to return goods within seven days and get a full refund.

sections.label: Consumer protection and CPFTA amendments
sections.summary: Appeals for greater consumer protection for advance payments and seeks an update on proposed amendments to the Consumer Protection Fair Trading Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This happened when a bridal shop closed last year and, recently, when a travel agency ceased operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I appeal to the Ministry to introduce greater consumer protection for consumers who have made advance payments to businesses in good faith, and then, these consumers find that when the business subsequently cease operations, they are left without recourse, except that they can make a claim as an unsecured creditor against a liquidator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Last year, I expressed concerns about the lack of teeth in the Consumer Protection Fair Trading Act (CPFTA) and for criminal action to be taken against dishonest traders or contractors who have cheated consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, may I seek an update on the proposed amendments to the CPFTA?

sections.label: Enterprise Development Fund fifth tranche
sections.summary: Announces that over the next five years the Government will set aside a grant budget of over S$2.3 billion under EDF 5 for local enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Government is monitoring this very closely and we stand ready to act when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that over the next five years, the Government will set aside a grant budget of over S$2.3 billion under the fifth tranche of the Enterprise Development Fund (EDF 5), specifically for the development of local enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This is a significant increase from the $1.4 billion approved under the previous tranche.

sections.label: IPG for SME IT
sections.summary: The $500-million IPG, introduced at Budget 2014 to accelerate SME take-up of IT solutions, will be enhanced in three ways.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The $500-million IPG was first introduced at Budget 2014 to accelerate the take-up of IT solutions by SMEs and this will be enhanced in three ways.

sections.label: SME Centre business advisors
sections.summary: In 2015, Business Advisors at the SME Centres reached out to more than 22,000 SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In 2015, our Business Advisors at the SME Centres reached out to more than 22,000 SMEs.

sections.label: Industrial, office and retail space
sections.summary: An average of 2.3 million square metres of industrial space will come on stream annually in the next two years, while office and retail rents fell 6.5% and 4.1% in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In the next two years, an average of 2.3 million square metres of industrial space will come on stream annually.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Similarly, for office and retail space, rents have fallen by 6.5% and 4.1% respectively in 2015, while a large supply of 993,000 square metres of office space and 808,000 square metres of retail space remains in the pipeline in the near future.

sections.label: Macro labour productivity growth
sections.summary: Between 2009 and 2015, labour productivity, measured by value-added per actual hour worked, grew by 2.7% per annum.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: At the macro level, between 2009 and 2015, labour productivity, as measured by value-added per actual hour worked, grew by 2.7% per annum.

sections.label: Outward and domestic productivity
sections.summary: From 2009 to 2015, labour productivity of outward-oriented sectors grew 5.1% per annum, while domestically-oriented sectors grew 0.8% per annum.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Overall, labour productivity of the outward-oriented sectors grew by 5.1% per annum from 2009 to 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: From 2009 to 2015, the labour productivity growth of these domestically-oriented sectors remained rather weak, at 0.8% per annum.

sections.label: Food manufacturers collective platform
sections.summary: The platform has helped Singapore food manufacturers benefit from collective branding, joint marketing and shared warehouses and logistics, with 40 food companies participating since its August 2015 launch.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This has helped Singapore food manufacturers benefit from the collective branding, joint marketing, as well as the sharing of warehouses and logistics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And since the platform's launch in August 2015, 40 food companies have participated in this initiative.

sections.label: JTC subletting policy and market share
sections.summary: JTC's subletting policy lets lessees sublet up to 30% of gross floor area, but JTC industrial space is only 8% of all industrial space.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In addition, Mr Chen Show Mao may wish to note that JTC's subletting policy provides companies with the flexibility to adjust their space usage according to business needs and supports space sharing by allowing lessees to sublet up to 30% of the total gross floor area to other companies for better synergy or to put temporarily unused space to better use.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: However, in terms of market share, JTC industrial space currently constitutes only 8% of all industrial space and we do not have the critical mass to influence overall market pricing.

sections.label: IE Singapore 2015 support numbers
sections.summary: In 2015 IE Singapore supported 34,000 companies, over 30,700 through MRA, and helped secure $769 million in trade and financing loans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Just to give some numbers, in 2015, IE Singapore supported 34,000 companies in their internationalisation efforts, and this is a 21% increase over 2014.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Through the MRA programme, more than 30,700 companies were supported, and the take-up rate of MRA grants increased by seven-fold over 2014, benefiting mainly SMEs with an annual turnover of below $5 million.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: IE Singapore also helped companies to secure $769 million in trade and financing loans in 2015, up from $753 million in 2014.

sections.label: TAC industry-upgrading projects support
sections.summary: As of March 2016, 35 TACs were supported for over 180 industry-upgrading projects, totalling over $120 million in grants for about 40,000 enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As of March 2016, 35 TACs have been supported for more than 180 industry-upgrading projects, totalling more than $120 million in grant and benefiting about 40,000 local enterprises.

sections.label: Franchising association Japan business meetings
sections.summary: The Franchising and Licensing Association (Singapore) organised 47 meetings in Japan for six companies, yielding 15 business leads and $530,000 in overseas sales.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Under this programme, the Franchising and Licensing Association (Singapore) organised 47 meetings in Japan for six companies, resulting in 15 business leads and overseas sales of $530,000.

sections.label: SPRING support for TAC secretariat
sections.summary: SPRING will support leadership training and second up to 20 public officers over five years to TACs, funding up to 70% of costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To strengthen the management of the TAC secretariat, SPRING will support training of the leadership team to manage corporate functions and also the secondment of up to 20 public officers over five years to TACs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: SPRING will support up to 70% of the cost of this secondment and development programmes.

sections.label: CPFTA injunction and prepayment protection
sections.summary: Proposed CPFTA enhancements include a stronger injunction framework and an administering agency, while consumers can protect prepayments via CaseTrust-accredited retailers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: First, our proposed enhancements to the CPFTA will include strengthening the injunction framework to prevent errant retailers from side-stepping injunction orders, and appointing an administering Government agency with investigation and enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Instead, consumers can protect their prepayments by choosing retailers that are CaseTrust-accredited.

sections.label: Solar adoption and SolarNova tenders
sections.summary: Solar adoption rose from 2 MWp in 2009 to 57 MWp in 2015, and SolarNova aggregates government solar demand through tenders.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Alongside improvements in the cost competitiveness of the technology, these have allowed solar adoption to rise from two megawatt peak (MWp) in 2009 to 57 MWp in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Under the SolarNova programme led by EDB and HDB, the Government is also taking the lead to accelerate solar deployment in Singapore by aggregating solar demand across various Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: HDB, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Public Utilities Board awarded a tender for an energy supplier to meet 76 MWp of combined demand in December last year, and tenders of 30 to 50 MWp sizes are expected to be launched around every nine months by HDB on behalf of the public agencies.

sections.label: Digital technologies global economic output
sections.summary: An Accenture report states increased digital technology use could add at least $1.36 trillion to global economic output in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: According to a report by Accenture, the increased use of digital technologies could add at least $1.36 trillion to the total global economic output in 2020.

sections.label: Assembly workers using advanced technologies
sections.summary: Operators in routine assembly work may have to master advanced technologies such as additive manufacturing and robotics solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Today, operators in routine assembly work may also have to master the use of advanced technologies, such as additive manufacturing and robotics solutions.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme
sections.summary: MTI supports the SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme, a work-study programme matching polytechnic and ITE graduates to companies including SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: To this end, MTI supports the SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme (ELP).

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: ELP is a work-study programme matching our fresh graduates from polytechnics and ITEs to suitable companies, including SMEs, in sectors related to their disciplines of study.

sections.label: YTP-Market Immersion Programme polytechnics
sections.summary: IE Singapore extended the YTP-Market Immersion Programme to polytechnics, and about 200 polytechnic students have gone to China, Germany, the US and ASEAN countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In November last year, IE Singapore officially extended the YTP-Market Immersion Programme to the polytechnics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Since then, about 200 polytechnic students have gone to China, Germany, the US and the ASEAN countries.

sections.label: Mentors and SMEs matched
sections.summary: Since its launch in December last year, 70 mentors have been qualified and 15 SMEs matched in sectors such as retail and engineering.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Since its launch in December last year, 70 mentors have been qualified and 15 SMEs have been matched in sectors, such as retail and engineering.

sections.label: Hotel SMP implementation partners
sections.summary: Hotel SMP strategies are implemented on the ground with STB, WDA, hotels, NTUC, FDAWU and SHA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The strategies under the Hotel SMP, for example, are being implemented on the ground in partnership with STB, the Workforce Development Agency, hotels, the National Trades Union Congress, the Food, Drinks and Allied Workers Union (FDAWU) and the Singapore Hotel Association (SHA).

sections.label: Tee Hai Chem employee sponsorship
sections.summary: Tee Hai Chem sponsors high-performing employees on part-time diploma studies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Take, for example, Tee Hai Chem, a local company that sponsors high-performing employees on part-time diploma studies.

sections.label: Romzi's PestBusters training and promotions
sections.summary: A 46-year-old PestBusters employee attended training courses, was promoted three times in six years, and will learn in Melbourne.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The 46-year-old employee at PestBusters has upgraded his knowledge and skills by attending several technical and WSQ training courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In just six years, Romzi has been promoted three times from a pest control technician to being an executive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And he does not intend to stop learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: He is keen to hone his craft with technology and has been selected to learn best practices in pest control work in Melbourne under Mediacorp's sponsorship.

sections.label: Cluster champions for sector transformation
sections.summary: The speaker applauds cluster champions from the public sector fast-tracking transformation of about 20 sectors covering about 80% of the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: Well, I applaud the Government's move to establish the cluster champions consisting of teams of officers from the public sector rolling up their sleeves and fast-tracking the transformation of about 20 sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: That is a tremendous effort, accounting for about 80% of our economy.

sections.label: Coordinated effort and cluster champions
sections.summary: The task requires coordinated effort across companies, TACs, Centres of Innovation and unions, with cluster champions appointed from Statutory Boards.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: As I stated, and as we all acknowledged, it is a major task and it will require a coordinated effort across various stakeholders – companies, TACs, Centres of Innovation and also in terms of the unions.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We will be appointing cluster champions from our various Statutory Boards for some of these key sectors.

sections.label: SBF target for HIPS
sections.summary: SBF's target is to get 30,000 of them onto HIPS by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: SBF's target is to get 30,000 of them onto HIPS by 2020.

sections.label: Japan TPP Diet ratification
sections.summary: The Japanese are proceeding to get TPP ratified in their Diet before July and the Upper House elections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
sentences.text: The good news is that the Japanese are proceeding to get TPP ratified in their Diet before July, before the Upper House's elections.

sections.label: TPP adds to US FTA
sections.summary: The TPP adds to the US-Singapore FTA by giving an FTA with Canada and Mexico and better market access through regional cumulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
sentences.text: As I had mentioned in my speech just now, although we have the bilateral US-Singapore FTA, the TPP adds on to this, because, for one, the TPP gives us a free trade agreement with Canada and Mexico, which we do not have bilateral FTAs with thus far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
sentences.text: But more importantly, the TPP gives us better market access because of regional cumulation.

sections.label: TPP ratification and RCEP pressure
sections.summary: If the TPP is not ratified, the speaker is concerned that pressure on RCEP may be lifted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
sentences.text: If we do not ratify the TPP, then I am very concerned that the pressure on RCEP may be lifted.
